All 57 aligned prose and list units carry a summary that matches the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in the spec's order (p01-p06, p07-p09, p10-p12, p13-p27 including p15a, p28-p31, p32-p36, p37, p37a/p39/p41/p42, p44-p50, p38, p51, p51a-p56). The reverse outline, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as sections[].paragraphs[]; no unit is missing, extra or out of order.

The outliner needed two phrases for this unit: keep a side-by-side full rebuild, and a table of every interaction's freshness, consistency, latency and availability. The sentence explaining the table states a claim about all five interactions (each has its own freshness and failure behaviour; the product page and the availability service stay the truth), which is not the paragraph's controlling idea (the full rebuild). The draft follows the spec, which attaches this table to p18 with a 'shows' that is a separate claim, so the second idea comes from the contract.

results.finding: The introduction opens on the declared intriguing example (the waterproof jacket whose rating is in a spreadsheet), then the copy premise, reviews, roadmap, scope and Eva's place in the order; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion opens by returning to the jacket, not with 'in conclusion'; it synthesizes, sorts the take-aways by how settled they are, gives questions and hands off; no new subtopic, no evidence that belongs in the body, no ending on a rephrased thesis alone.

It states what no single section states: the jacket, the stale 'in stock', the outlived rule and the lost review are one kind of fault, and the conditions that prevent it are owned outside the search team; so what: the first money goes to attributes and a stock feed, with the 9.4% to 4.1% fall on the same engine. (The breadth of 'three conditions prevent it' is recorded under flow_is_followable.)

'The chapter opened with a waterproof jacket that a search could not find because its rating existed only in a spreadsheet' returns to the declared callback, and 'no ranking algorithm could have found the jacket; an attribute and a synonym did' answers the opening's claim.

The intro reader predicted every roadmap promise in order: the Kestrel & Pine report, the three ways and vocabulary, the index as a copy with its three conditions, ordering and filtering, AI retrieval, wholesale, reviews, the product comparison by scale stage and vendor documentation, and the failures with detection and recovery. It predicted the Kestrel & Pine case, vendor documentation and EU and US review rules as evidence and a plain, practical tone; it did not name usability research, which the introduction does not signal, a minor gap.

The reader names a data gap (shell-jacket title, rating in a spreadsheet, indexed fields title/description/type/tags), a missing synonym per language and an unindexed product, and checks the zero-result rate and top failing queries per language, the indexed fields and synonym sets before any new engine; matches expected.

The reader recommends only a coarse 'available' flag in the index, with the exact answer from the availability service at query time, because an indexed fact is only as fresh as the last indexing run while stock changes by the second, citing the two-hour Phantom Stock; matches expected.

The reader says each review must keep how it was collected and, if verified, the order it came from, because Directive (EU) 2019/2161 makes purchaser origin material information and requires reasonable steps to check; matches expected.
